title: Binary operations, semigroups, and monoids
section: Part B: Abstract Algebra ▷ Binary Structures and the Definition of a Group
terms: binary operation; closure; associativity; binary structure; semigroup; monoid; identity.

exposition.text:
A binary operation on S is a function S × S → S; closure and being defined on every ordered pair
are built into the definition. An associative binary operation makes S a semigroup. A two-sided
identity e satisfies ea = ae = a for all a; a semigroup with identity is a monoid. A two-sided
identity, if present, is unique.
These properties must be checked for the specified set and operation. Subtraction is closed on
Z but not associative; addition on positive integers is associative but has no identity in that set.
A table in which each symbol occurs once in each row and column need not be associative, so
that condition alone does not prove a group.
A nonempty set together with a specified binary operation is a binary structure. A right iden-
tity satisfies x ∗ e = x and a left identity satisfies e ∗ x = x; either property alone need not
give uniqueness. Cancellation means ax = ay ⇒ x = y and xa = ya ⇒ x = y. Every finite
cancellative monoid is a group, by repetition of powers, but finiteness is essential.

question.text:
On R, define x ∗ y = x + y + xy. Which description is correct?
(A) Not closed
(B) Closed but not associative
(C) An associative operation with no identity
(D) A monoid that is not a group
(E) A group

solution.text:
The identity is 0, and 1 + (x ∗y) = (1 +x)(1+ y) proves associativity. However, (−1)∗ y = −1
for every y, so −1 has no inverse. Thus the structure is a monoid but not a group.

question.text:
A finite monoid satisfies both cancellation laws. Which conclusion must hold?
(A) It is a group.
(B) It is commutative.
(C) Its order is prime.
(D) Every element is its own inverse.
(E) It has at most two elements.

question.text:
On a set S with at least two elements define x ∗ y = x. Which description is correct?
(A) The operation is not associative.
(B) Every element is a two-sided identity.
(C) Every element is a right identity, but no left identity exists.
(D) Every element is a left identity, but no right identity exists.
(E) It is a group.

solution.text:
Both (x ∗ y) ∗ z and x ∗ (y ∗ z) equal x, so the operation is associative. Also x ∗ e = x for any
e, making every element a right identity. A left identity would need e ∗ x = e = x for every
x, impossible on a set with at least two elements. Identity uniqueness concerns two-sided
identities.

question.text:
On {0, 1, 2} define x ∗ y ≡ −x − y (mod 3). Each row and column of its operation table contains
all three elements. Which statement is true?
(A) The structure must be a group.
(B) The operation is associative but has no identity.
(C) The operation is not associative.
(D) The operation is not closed.
(E) The identity is zero.

A binary operation on a nonempty set has an element l with l ∗ x = x for all x, and an element r
with x ∗ r = x for all x. Associativity is not assumed. Which conclusion follows?
(A) l = r, and this element is a two-sided identity.
(B) The operation is associative.
(C) The operation is commutative.
(D) Every element has an inverse.
(E) l and r must be distinct.

solution.text:
Evaluating l ∗ r by the left-identity property gives r, and by the right-identity property gives
l. Hence l = r, and the common element has both properties. This proof does not use asso-
ciativity.
